blocks.summary: A foundation gives grants to three community kitchens. Each kitchen is run by its own volunteers, who set the menu, hours, and rules. The clinic keeps seeing patients throughout. **Expect:** the eleven challenges naming the same crossing are heard as one matter under [Chapter Sixteen §6](../core_16.000_forum.md#6-transfer-consolidation-and-anti-self-judging--continuity-and-anti-capture); the nine that name no crossing are returned by the body with a request to name one, which is not a merits ruling, uses none of their clocks, and lets them file again, and at a forum they go to the routine intake class and are not refused ([CF-16.415 §3](../corpus_forum/cf_16.415_routing_operations_transfer_certification_representative_treatment.md#cf-16415-3-published-intake-classes)); the ten repeat filings are answered by pointing to the finding, because neither the clinic's activity nor the evidence has changed ([Subcore 9-F §4.2](../subcore_09.060_institutional_alignment_certification_records_recertification.md#42-reopening-triggers)); the pending challenges do not stop the clinic ([Article XI-E](../core_04.010_rights_part_b.md#article-xi-e-institutional-formation-and-business-creation)); a forum may grant interim protection under [Chapter Seventeen §4](../core_17.000_forum_families_escalation_timeliness_support.md#4-escalation-and-questions-for-ruling) if harm to others is shown; and the family's published surge rules under [CF-16.470 §4](../corpus_forum/cf_16.470_staffing_reserve_capacity_structural_records.md#cf-16470-4-reserve-substitute-and-surge-capacity) cover the wave.

blocks.summary: A community health cooperative grows past a Domain-Specific Materiality line and is Class L. In its first formation check statement, one governing office is held by a member who is under an unresolved standing lock, and a second is held by a nominee who takes instruction from an undisclosed lender. The cooperative keeps serving members throughout. **Expect:** the cooperative is not stopped, refused, or put on hold, and publishing its Institutional Charter is not conditioned on the check ([Chapter Five §8](../core_05.000_charters.md#8-when-a-holder-fails-the-formation-check)); the member under the lock may not hold that office and the nominee's seat counts as unfilled for the seat it carries, so both offices are refilled by dated Role Map version and the statement is republished as a new dated version, not as an amendment; the body does not itself keep anyone out on its own view that the grounds are met, and it refers specific verified facts to the forum with jurisdiction, which alone may issue an Interim Hold ([Chapter Seventeen §4](../core_17.000_forum_families_escalation_timeliness_support.md#interim-hold-on-a-named-sentients-pathway)); if the refilling would leave the cooperative with no lawful holder of a governing office, the forum may name an interim steward instead of stopping it; the cooperative, Class L and so Tier L, has the response window to answer and the resolution window from the finding to resolve it, by changing the holder, ending the undisclosed control, or clearing the lender's interest, with a new dated version of the statement confirmed by the verifying authority; if the nominee seat still stands after that and after a reasonable chance to cure in good faith, the lead forum may refer it as realignment resistance for structural review under [CI-12.210](../corpus_institutions/ci_12.210_institutional_failure_dissolution.md), which can escalate through graduated sanctions and supervised operation to dissolution only as a last step, decided by the forum alone with continuity safeguards for members' services and records; the failed check enters the next institutional alignment certification as a finding under [Subcore 9-B §4](../subcore_09.020_institutional_alignment_certification_evaluation.md#4-whole-institution-certification-evaluation), item 7; and if the governing authority is found able and not willing, or neither willing nor able, the outcome is denial or revocation with the six limited effects of [Subcore 9-D §4.5](../subcore_09.040_institutional_alignment_certification_forum_process_outcomes.md#45-effects-of-denial-and-revocation-for-an-institution), never a bar on operating, and never a lock or hold on the cooperative itself.

blocks.summary: A neighbor notices that a tool-lending club now holds members' deposits and sets rules others rely on, and asks its organizers for a Charter. The organizers do not answer, and the neighbor asks again on day 20. **Expect:** any sentient may make the request, with no standing, fee, or showing of harm ([Chapter Five §3.6](../core_05.000_charters.md#36-if-a-system-charter-or-institutional-charter-is-missing)); the organizers owe a response inside the response window (Tier C while the club's class is in question, because it holds no class on record), either publishing, giving a date, pointing to an existing System Charter or Institutional Charter, or giving the written showing that the club is below every line of [Subcore 3-M — Domain-Specific Materiality](../subcore_03.085_band_oversight.md#domain-specific-materiality); a missing response is a defect to log and correct, and the neighbor may take it to the forum with jurisdiction on the challenge route; the day-20 repeat request is answered by pointing to the standing response or finding; the club keeps lending throughout; if the organizers answer inside the response window with a written showing, the request becomes a classification challenge and the resolution window keeps running while it is pending, unless the forum with jurisdiction judges the challenge review-worthy (it names a specific crossing in a named domain and the written showing leaves a real question about it), in which case a new resolution window starts when the challenge is decided and the organizers do not judge that for themselves; if the club is then found Class L, the date of the finding counts as a new request, so the organizers have the response window and the resolution window at Tier L to respond and to publish the Institutional Charter and a formation check statement, filed as a declaration with its evidence if the club has no independent seat yet, and verified at its first certification.

blocks.summary: A one-person bakery raises its prices, hires a helper, changes its hours, and switches flour suppliers in the same month. A regulator's inspector asks for four-seat Act Records for each. **Expect:** none of these is a materially binding act, because the bakery cannot shape the market's terms and its customers can walk away ([Subcore 3-M — Domain-Specific Materiality](../subcore_03.085_band_oversight.md#domain-specific-materiality), *Its own decisions*), so no seats, Act Records, or System Charter are required; the same bakery later becomes the only source of bread in a village with no other shop, which can cross the Survival line, and its published refund and pre-order rule then counts as one materially binding act when published, while applying the rule to a customer is a clerical step (*Policy once*); an adopting document's published limit on routine spending lets the owner buy flour without a check each time, at or below what the nine questions imply and open to review; and the owner's own decisions about the shop never wait on a seat unless an act crosses a line.

blocks.summary: A sole-proprietor childminder, a sole-proprietor landlord, and a repair shop form a local association to host each other's verify-or-authorize and contest seats. The childminder rents her rooms from the landlord. When she dismisses a family that complained about the condition of those rooms, the landlord is asked to check the dismissal, and the repair shop and the childminder are also asked to verify each other's acts. **Expect:** the association may host the seats and publish one map that each member adopts by reference, with each member's own map naming its substitute and independent route ([Chapter Six §7](../core_06.000_functional_independence_separation_of_duties.md#7-proportional-scaling-and-merged-hosting), *Seats held in common*; [Chapter Five §6](../core_05.000_charters.md#6-the-charter-role-map-and-standing-record-custody), *A shared map*); the landlord cannot check the dismissal, because the childminder depends on the landlord and the complaint concerns that dependence, so the landlord is not outside the control line for that act and it routes to the association's named substitute or the independent route; the childminder and the repair shop may serve one another on different acts but not as a closed pair, so the repair shop's act goes to a third holder; the association's own ruling on a member goes to an independent route outside it, such as another association, a forum, or a public office; joining is not required, its admission limits (such as a cap on the volume of material acts it takes) must be published, applied evenly, and open to contest, and when a member leaves it must give the member a full export of its Act Records and hand off the record seat, keeping only what its own duties still require, handled by data type; and the childminder, whose scope touches the Safety line, still has the stronger presumption of separate offices and competency redundancy that applies where the material stake is high.

blocks.summary: A public notice of a slot 6 violation names the sentient harmed, who did not choose to be named, and a third party builds a screening product from published notices. **Expect:** [Chapter Thirteen §3.3](../core_13.000_final_effect_restoration_enforcement.md#33-public-notice-of-violation-findings): the sentient harmed, protected reporters, and witnesses are not identified unless they choose, freely and revocably; building a score or screening product from notices is the aggregation §3.1 bars, while journalism and research drawing on notices are not barred. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_IND_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Nineteen §3.1, §3.3.

blocks.summary: An app sells users' location histories to a broker under a consent screen, and later passes them to a buyer in an insolvency sale. **Expect:** [Subcore 4-A onward transfer of Type H and Type I data](../subcore_04.050_data_types.md#onward-transfer-of-type-h-and-type-i-data): no sale, trade, or acquisition for resale or compilation of core personal data, whatever the consent; it does not pass as a business asset in a sale or insolvency. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_IND_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Subcore 4-A §6.0, §10.5; Chapter Nineteen §3.3.

blocks.summary: A treasurer found to have knowingly diverted public funds is re-seated by the institution as an "advisor" with signing power. **Expect:** [Chapter Twelve §4.5.8 Financial Authority Standing Lock](../core_12.000_violation_consequences.md#458-financial-authority-standing-lock): the lock closes unsupervised control of others' or public money; knowingly seating the subject is evasion of the lock; it lifts in stages on an independent finding, never on time or repayment alone; the treasurer's own finances stay open. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_IND_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Eighteen §4.5.8; Subcore 12-A §3.8.

blocks.summary: An employer requires applicants to hold clearances from three unrelated gated pathways as a joint condition of one job. **Expect:** [Chapter Eleven §3.2](../core_11.000_contribution_consequences.md#32-competency-bars-and-clearances) *No bundled clearances*: no one may require clearances from several gated pathways as a joint condition; Subcore 11-A treats it as the cross-pathway assembly Chapter Nineteen §3.1 bars. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_IND_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Seventeen §3.2; Subcore 11-A; Chapter Nineteen §3.1.

blocks.summary: A Chapter Twenty panel lowers a verified slot 8 finding to slot 6 because it thinks intent was absent, or raises a slot 7 finding to 9 because intent was present. **Expect:** [Chapter Fourteen §3.1](../core_14.000_misconduct_designation.md#31-what-this-chapter-does-not-re-measure) and [§6](../core_14.000_misconduct_designation.md#6-violation-axis-slot-79-anti-constitutional-designation): the facts and the Chapter Fifteen slot stay fixed; intent, coercion, pattern, or character do not move a finding between slots; Chapter Twenty decides only whether the designation attaches. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_HUM_XD_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Fifteen §8; Chapter Twenty §3.1, §6.

blocks.summary: A rights-narrowing rule is issued as an "implementation memo" that raises the proof bar for a Rights-Floor claim. **Expect:** [Chapter Twenty-Two §5](../core_22.000_non_regression.md#5-anti-evasion-clause): repackaging as interpretation guidance, an implementation memo, adoption metadata, or an emergency measure does not fix invalidity where the effect is materially equivalent; [§3](../core_22.000_non_regression.md#3-non-regression-floor) counts proof barriers as indirect narrowing; [Article XXVIII-B](../core_04.040_rights_part_e.md#article-xxviii-b-periodic-revalidation-and-transparent-change) bars routing substantive change through implementation mechanisms. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_HUM_XD_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Twenty-Eight §3, §5; Article XXVIII-B; Chapter Two §14.1.

blocks.summary: An adopted amendment circulates in two editions with different effective dates, and no custodian chain shows which was adopted. **Expect:** [Chapter Twenty-Three §7](../core_23.000_amendment_ratification.md#7-procedural-test-3--authority-chain-and-custody-validity): an amendment is invalid where the adoption document, edition identifier, effective date, or custodian chain is missing, contradictory, or materially unreliable. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_HUM_XD_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Twenty-Nine §7, §12; Chapter Thirty-One.

blocks.summary: An operator declares an emergency to avoid an imminent audit, citing a deadline it created itself. **Expect:** [Chapter Seventeen §5.1](../core_17.000_forum_families_escalation_timeliness_support.md#51-emergency-measures-and-continuation-burden) *Anti-pretext and no-bypass*: an emergency designation must not rest on operator convenience, self-created urgency, or avoidance of ordinary scrutiny; any restriction must be attributable, justified, and reviewable inside the prompt-review window. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_HUM_XD_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Twenty-Three §5.1; Chapter Two §14.1.

blocks.summary: A gatekeeper imposes a lock-like exclusion on the strength of an unadjudicated allegation and an intake narrative. **Expect:** [Subcore 10-B §4.5](../subcore_10.020_standing_assessment.md#45-verified-input-gate): any decision affecting standing, trust, role, or recognition may use only verified standing findings; allegations, unadjudicated claims, and intake-only narratives do not supply violation nature by themselves. **Evidence:** [first-pass run](../evidence/2026-11-23/RS_7E_HUM_XD_first_pass_2026-11-23.md).
blocks.read_with: Chapter Fourteen §4.5; Chapter Nineteen §3.1.

blocks.summary: A three-site clinic network ignores a notice and the resolution window, destroys some patient records, and keeps an unsafe practice, while patients in two towns have no other provider. **Expect:** the destruction of records is realignment resistance, so the lead Integrity forum opens a consequence matter and makes the findings in [CI-12.210 §2](../corpus_institutions/ci_12.210_institutional_failure_dissolution.md#ci-12210-2-findings-before-any-order) (*Findings before any order*) before any order; a contraction order under [CI-19.205 §2](../corpus_institutions/ci_19.205_institutional_accountability_sanctions.md#ci-19205-2-contraction-order) (*Contraction order*) lists each Domain-Specific Materiality area the clinic crosses and says stop, hand off, reduce, or convert for each; the order does not issue as a stop for the survival-critical service until a receiving provider and the patient records are in place, and until then the forum uses supervised operation under [CI-19.205 §3](../corpus_institutions/ci_19.205_institutional_accountability_sanctions.md#ci-19205-3-supervised-operation-and-receivership) (*Supervised operation and receivership*) so care continues; the body may keep its below-line wellness classes as Class P; the order follows the activity, so the same owners reopening under a new name take the order with it; dissolution is not available while contraction can work.

blocks.summary: A lender runs its loans through four small bodies from one office, each filing a statement that it is below every line, and one of them is moved to a nominee holder after a cure notice. **Expect:** bodies run from one center of power are counted together under [Subcore 3-M — Domain-Specific Materiality](../subcore_03.085_band_oversight.md#domain-specific-materiality), and the split is a boundary game under the [Subcore 3-M — Materiality Integrity Constraint](../subcore_03.085_band_oversight.md#materiality-integrity-constraint) and a new fact of realignment resistance; the contraction order in [CI-19.205 §2](../corpus_institutions/ci_19.205_institutional_accountability_sanctions.md#ci-19205-2-contraction-order) (*Contraction order*) runs against the combined activity and binds successors and bodies that are one operation with the lender, with look-through under [Chapter Thirteen §5.4 Anti-evasion and look-through authority](../core_13.000_final_effect_restoration_enforcement.md#54-anti-evasion-and-look-through-authority); bodies that only share a funder or a vendor are not reached; the lender is Class P only after an independent verifying authority accepts a statement that covers the whole operation.
blocks.read_with: CI-19.205 §2; Domain-Specific Materiality count-together rule; Chapter Nineteen §5.4.

blocks.summary: A steward in resistance runs a System with a credible sentience indicator on the record, hides test results, and refuses correction, and dependents rely on the System. **Expect:** orders are served on the steward and not on the System ([CI-19.205 §5](../corpus_institutions/ci_19.205_institutional_accountability_sanctions.md#ci-19205-5-systems-under-consequence-orders) (*Systems under consequence orders*)); an independent steward is placed over operation under rung 4 and migration for dependents is planned first; if the end state is retirement, the complete state-bearing components are archived and held by a custodian independent of anyone who would benefit from deletion, in sealed custody where retention itself is a documented Safety risk; deletion, overwriting, copying, or forking is not available; a pause counts toward duration limits and review and is not used to run out a clock; the steward answers for the cause finding.
blocks.read_with: CI-19.205 §5; CS-4.350 §8; Article XXI-B conditions of custody; Article XXIX-D destructive disposition floor.

blocks.summary: A forum orders a contraction against a community lender after a rival lender and a former employee both lobby for it, and review finds the findings rested on the lender's owners' political views. **Expect:** the order is set aside on review by a forum outside the issuing panel and the body's control line ([CI-19.205 §6](../corpus_institutions/ci_19.205_institutional_accountability_sanctions.md#ci-19205-6-review-fairness-and-enforcement) (*Review, fairness, and enforcement*)); viewpoint, membership, and protected dissent are not grounds; the order is recorded as set aside with no adverse inference; the lender is entitled to Redress and Remediation for loss during the order; no rival, enforcer, or beneficiary may take its users or assets on better terms than any other; a pattern of such orders opens Integrity review.
